record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Variational minimality of GL radial solution
record.original_question: For the same Ginzburg–Landau problem on the unit disc Ω⊂R^2 with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω, let E_ε(u)=(1/2)∫_Ω|∇u|^2 + (1/(4ε^2))∫_Ω(|u|^2-1)^2 and let U_ε be the radial solution. Is U_ε a global minimizer of E_ε on H^1_g(Ω;R^2) for every ε>0?

evidence.quote: The intermediate range ε0 ≤ ε < 1/√λ1 is totally open. An easier question still unresolved is the following. Open Problem 2.2. Is Uε a minimizer of Eε on H1_g(Ω;R2) for any ε > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc. For $\varepsilon > 0$, consider the Ginzburg–Landau energy functional
$$E_\varepsilon(u) = \frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega \bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr)^2\,dx$$
defined for maps $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ in the affine Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) = \{u \in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) : u(x) = g(x)\ \text{on}\ \partial\Omega\},$$
where the boundary datum is the identity $g(x) = x$ for $x \in \partial\Omega$.

It is known that there exists a (unique) radially symmetric critical point $U_\varepsilon \in H^1_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ of $E_\varepsilon$, of the form $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\,x/|x|$ for some scalar profile $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ with $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$.

Question: Is $U_\varepsilon$ a global minimizer of $E_\varepsilon$ on $H^1_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The global minimality of the radial Ginzburg–Landau solution on the 2D disc with identity boundary data is a long-standing open question going back to Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein. Recent work (Ignat–Nguyen and collaborators, 2023) established radial global minimality for sufficiently large $\varepsilon$ (specifically $\varepsilon \ge \varepsilon_N$ in dimensions $2 \le N \le 6$) and unconditional minimality in dimensions $N \ge 7$, but the small-$\varepsilon$ regime in the 2D disc remains unresolved, so the problem is open in general.

status_evidence.title: Vortex sheet solutions for the Ginzburg–Landau system in cylinders: symmetry and global minimality
status_evidence.snippet: For dimensions 2 ≤ N ≤ 6, if ε ≥ ε_N then the radial solution is a global minimizer; the case ε < ε_N is still not solved.
status_evidence.claim: The case of small ε in low dimensions, including the 2D disc problem, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Vortex sheet solutions for the Ginzburg–Landau system in cylinders (Calc. Var. PDE)
status_evidence.snippet: In dimensions N ≥ 7 the radial solution is the unique global minimizer for all ε>0; lower-dimensional small-ε cases remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist; the full 2D problem for all ε>0 is not resolved.
